text:
Alex Chen: nightly GPU smoke turned red on h100-canary, 3/4 shards failing. https://ci.internal.redwood/12345 :confused:
Jamie Patel: saw it. errors look like 'invalid device function' + a warmup OOM on shard-2
Samir Rao: can you paste the top of the log?
Alex Chen: pasted snippet:
```
E //runtime: cuda kernel load failed: invalid device function
2026-03-17T08:12:45Z [pid=2345] Alloc failed: size=1.1GiB, free=900MiB
RuntimeVersion: runtime 520, driver 515
```
Morgan Li: that runtime/driver skew screams PTX JIT mismatch. we recently rolled a subset of hosts to driver 525 but canary should be 520 still
Kai: also note the OOM during warmup — we've seen allocation spikes on certain model warmups that push beyond requested memory; might be multi-job interference
Samir Rao: quick triage plan: 1) rerun failing matrix on explicit driver tag 2) run compat check across driver 515/520/525 3) if still flaky, bisect PRs touching allocator in last 48h
Alex Chen: queueing rerun on pool=h100-canary with env GPU_WARMUP_OFF=1 to isolate warmup OOM
infra-bot: rerun triggered: job 23346 on h100-canary (driver=520) — tracking: https://ci.internal.redwood/23346
Jamie Patel: if rerun passes with WARMUP_OFF, then warmup alloc spike is likely; if it fails with invalid device function, it's driver/runtime mismatch 
Morgan Li: I'll check fleet rollout logs for driver changes in the last 24h and post here
Morgan Li: fleet shows a partial rollout to a subset (cluster us-west-2-g) to 525 at 02:00 UTC — might be causing cross-pool scheduling mixing nodes
Kai: can someone run `nvidia-smi -q | grep 'Driver Version'` from the failing node?
Alex Chen: attached output from failing node:
```
Driver Version                        : 525.60.11
CUDA Version                          : 12.2
```
Jamie Patel: aha. container runtime was built with toolkit/runtime 520 image, node drifted to 525 -> invalid device function possible due to compiled cubin vs driver
Samir Rao: temporary mitigation: pin jobs to pool with matching driver or force container to build PTX at runtime by setting `FORCE_PTX_COMPILE=1` in the job env
Alex Chen: infra-bot rerun finished: shard-0 pass, shard-1 fail (invalid device fn), shard-2 fail (OOM), shard-3 pass
infra-bot: summary: 2/4 failed — details: https://ci.internal.redwood/23346/summary
Jamie Patel: next steps: - Morgan, can you roll back the partial driver rollout or quarantine nodes in us-west-2-g? - I'll open a short PR to add a quick guard in the CI scheduler to prefer exact-driver pools for h100 jobs
Morgan Li: rolling back the 525 subset now to 520 on the affected machines, will monitor
Kai: also adding a transient skip label to the flaky test: //tests/gpu/smoke:quant_smoke until we confirm root cause 
Alex Chen: starting a bisect across recent allocator/driver-related commits if rollback doesn't stabilize. ping me if you need test access
Samir Rao: FYI for next time: run `bazel test //infra/compat:gpu_driver_matrix --config=canary` before a large rollout
Jamie Patel: opening the scheduler guard PR (small) and will add doc notes about driver-pin tags for CI pools
Alex Chen: thanks y'all. will update when rollback status is confirmed. :thumbsup:
Morgan Li: rollback successful on 6 machines, monitoring smoke jobs now
infra-bot: new run triggered: job 23349 — all shards queued on driver-520 nodes
Alex Chen: job 23349 passed all shards. looks like driver skew was the main culprit. leaving bisect on hold.
Jamie Patel: reopening if we see OOM reoccurrence; otherwise close the incident tomorrow after postmortem note
Alex Chen: agreed. I'll draft a quick postmortem and link here.
Jamie Patel: thanks everyone for the quick turnaround :raised_hands:
